title: Home Insurance in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **The sum insured decides everything, not the premium.** The German benchmark is **650 euro per square metre** of living space. For the average Berlin rented flat of 68.2 square metres that is **44,330 euro**.

**Insure below that and every claim is cut in the same proportion**, from the first euro, even when only part of the flat was hit. Insure at the benchmark and you normally get the **Unterversicherungsverzicht**, which waives the cut.
**Berlin 2025: 10,618 home burglaries, up 24.5 percent**, average loss **8,832 euro**, and only **7.9 percent** of cases cleared. Cellar break-ins were far more common at **18,421**.

**The bike clause is the weak one.** Theft away from the flat is an add-on capped at about **one to two percent** of the sum insured. One percent of an average Berlin flat is **443 euro** against an average stolen bike worth **1,246 euro**.
**Check for the Nachtzeitklausel.** Older contracts only pay for a bike taken between **22:00 and 06:00** if it was inside the flat, the cellar or a locked bike room.

**Liability matters more than contents in a rented flat.** Privathaftpflicht from roughly **40 to 120 euro a year** for one person, at least **10 million euro** of cover, and it must include **Mietsachschaeden** and **loss of other people’s keys**.

**The notice period is three months before the end of your insurance year.** On a calendar-year contract that is **30 September**. Raising the sum insured, though, is an amendment you can ask for any day.
